title: Rotating-wave approximation for spin-boson models with structured fields
authors: Aitor Balmaseda, Davide Lonigro, Juan Manuel Pérez-Pardo
abstract: We derive state-dependent bounds on the difference between two quantum evolutions generated by unbounded Hamiltonians sharing a common form domain. The main technical tool is a second integration by parts, performed at the level of sesquilinear forms rather than at the operator level, which removes the need for a common invariant operator domain. The resulting estimate involves the norm of the time-integrated difference of the two generators, rather than the integral of its norm, and is therefore sensitive to the averaging effects produced by fast-oscillating terms. As an application we prove a quantitative bound on the rotating-wave approximation for spin-boson models with a structured boson field, described by an arbitrary massive dispersion relation on a general measure space and by a suitable class of form factors. The proof involves a careful analysis of the high-frequency scaling. The bound holds on a dense subspace of states, is fully explicit, and all the constants entering it depend only on the parameters of the model and not on the frequency scale, so that the approximation becomes exact in the limit of large frequency.
summary: This paper develops rigorous mathematical techniques to bound the error incurred when using the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA) in spin-boson models. By employing advanced analysis on sesquilinear forms, the authors derive an explicit error bound that confirms the RWA's accuracy in the high-frequency limit. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for analyzing quantum dynamics in structured environments.
main_problem: The paper rigorously derives quantitative, state-dependent error bounds for the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA) when applied to spin-boson models with structured boson fields.
main_result: It establishes an explicit error bound showing the RWA error vanishes as $O(\alpha^{-1})$ in the large-frequency limit, confirming the approximation's accuracy under specific mathematical conditions.
method: The core method involves developing advanced mathematical tools, specifically using a second integration by parts at the level of sesquilinear forms, to control the difference between two quantum evolutions generated by different Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the spin-boson model, which describes the interaction between a two-level quantum system (spin) and a bosonic field. The Hamiltonian comparison is between the full model and its RWA counterpart.
key_observables: The primary observable is the difference between the unitary propagators, $\lVert U_{	ext{RWA}}(t, s) - U(t, s) Vert$, quantified by explicit error bounds.
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to the large-frequency parameter ($\alpha$) and the structure of the boson field, characterized by its form factor and dispersion relation.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on advanced functional analysis, including the ability to perform integration by parts on sesquilinear forms and assuming the initial state lies in sufficiently high-regularity domains.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing general mathematical tools for bounding differences between quantum evolutions (using sesquilinear forms) to applying these tools specifically to derive the quantitative RWA error bound for the spin-boson model.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, quantitative framework for analyzing approximations like the RWA, which is fundamental in quantum optics and open quantum systems, especially when dealing with complex, structured environments.
